Title: Sparse Gradient Echoes in Low-Rank Adapters

Authors:Lena Vasquez, Oskar Brandt
Abstract: We study how gradient updates in low-rank adapters interact with the frozen weights they modify, and we find that a small set of directions recurs across tasks, steps, and random seeds. We call these recurring directions gradient echoes. Across six language and vision benchmarks, fewer than two percent of adapter coordinates carry more than half of the cumulative update norm, and the same coordinates are selected again when training restarts from scratch. Building on this observation, we propose EchoPrune, a method that identifies echo coordinates during the first few hundred steps and freezes the rest, reducing optimizer memory by a factor of four while matching full adapter accuracy within half a point. We also show that echoes transfer between related tasks, which suggests that they reflect structure in the pretrained model rather than in any single dataset.
Comments:14 pages, 6 figures
